paper.title: A Biased Graph Neural Network Sampler with Near-Optimal Regret

settings.name_in_paper: GNN neighbor sampling as non-oblivious adversarial multiple-play bandit with variation budget (worst-case regret with dynamic oracle)
unmapped: Rewards are non-oblivious: they depend on the learner's past sampling actions and on GCN training (SGD) dynamics; the variation budget V_T = C_v ln T is derived from GCN training assumptions (Lipschitz activation, bounded weights, bounded gradients, learning rate 1/t)
Arms are the D_v neighbors of a node (K = D_v); k neighbors sampled per round
Rewards bounded in absolute value by C_r = 3 C_z^2 (rescaled bounded range)
settings.definition_quote: \Reg(\T) = \sum_{t=1}^{\T} \sum_{i\in\Nkstar} \E[\rl_{i,t}] - \sum_{t=1}^{\T} \sum_{\It\in\Nst} \E^{\pi} [\rl_{\It,t}]. where \Nkstar = \argmax_{\Nk\subset\Nv} \sum_{i\in\Nk} \E[\rl_{i,t}], |\Nkstar| = \kk. Because we consider the non-oblivious adversary, \E[\rl_{i,t}] is taken over the randomness of rewards caused by the previous history of randomized arm pulling.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial multiple-play bandit (weak regret with static oracle), rewards bounded by C_r
unmapped: Rewards bounded above by C_r (r_tilde <= C_r, nonnegative via ReLU); regret compares expected rewards over the action trajectory against best fixed k-subset

symbols.C_bar: constant (2 sqrt(2 k C_r (e^{C_r}-1)) + 2k) C_v^{1/3}, independent of K and T
symbols.C_v: variation budget constant, V_T = C_v ln T

conditions: variation budget V_T = C_v ln T (Lemma 2), from GCN assumptions: Lipschitz activation with sigma(0)=0, bounded weight spectral norms, bounded gradients, SGD learning rate alpha_t = 1/t
K = D_v is the degree of the root node; k neighbors sampled per round
tuning: gamma = min{1, sqrt((exp(C_r)-1) K ln(K/k) / (2 k C_r T))}

source.label: the:main_theorem
source.quote: Consider Algorithm~\ref{alg:our_sampler} as the neighbor sampling algorithm for training GCN. Given either \eqref{eq:our_reward} or \eqref{eq:our_practical_reward} as reward function, we can bound its regret as follows. Let $ \DeltaT = (\Cv \ln\T)^{-\frac{2}{3}} (\K\ln\K)^{\frac{1}{3}} \T^{\frac{2}{3}} $, ... for every $ \T \geq \K \geq 2 $, we have the regret bound ... $\Reg(\T) \leq \Cba (\K\ln\K)^{\frac{1}{3}} \cdot (\T \sqrt{\ln\T})^{\frac{2}{3}}$ where $ \Cba $ is a absolute constant independent with $ \K $ and $ \T $.

results.notes: Paper's D_v (degree) mapped to K, sample size k to m (C_bar depends on k). Regret is against the per-round best k-subset of expected rewards (dynamic oracle) under a non-oblivious adversary with variation budget; holds for both the biased reward and its ReLU practical version.

symbols.C_r: upper bound on the rewards, r_tilde <= C_r

conditions: k = m arms selected per round out of K
tuning: gamma = min{1, sqrt((exp(C_r)-1) K ln(K/k) / (2 k C_r T))}

source.label: lem:weak_regret
source.quote: Given the reward function $ \rlt_{i,t} \leq \Cr $, set $ \eta = ... $ and $ \gamma = ... $. Then, we have the regret bound for Exp3.M as: \hReg(\T) = \max_{\Nk\subset [\K]} \sum_{t=1}^{\T} \sum_{j\in \Nk} \E[\rtl_{j,t}] - \sum_{t=1}^{\T} \sum_{\It \in \Nst}\E^{\pi} [\rtl_{\It, t}] \leq \sqrt{2\kk\Cr(\exp(\Cr)-1)} \sqrt{\K\T\ln(\K/\kk)}

results.notes: Adaptation of Uchiya et al. (2010) Theorem 2 to reward scale C_r; weak regret against best fixed k-subset in expectation. Environment set to adversarial_adaptive since expectations are over the action trajectory with non-oblivious rewards; proof implicitly uses nonnegative rewards.
